issues.detail: The Hebrew 'טְמֵאַת הַנִּדָּה עִנּוּ בָךְ' means 'they humbled/afflicted the woman unclean through menstruation in you' (i.e., they violated the menstruous woman). The Chinese '玷污了不潔之物' ('defiled the unclean thing') misidentifies the object as an inanimate thing rather than a person (the menstruous woman), and omits the explicit subject 'they' (implied in the verb עִנּוּ) and the verb's sense of afflicting/humbling a person. This changes who is doing what to whom.
